Let
\[
A_i=-I+N_i,\qquad 
N_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&a\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
N_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ b&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Write \(z(t)=e^{-t}x(t)\). Then \(x\) satisfies
\[
\dot x(t)=N_{\sigma(t)}x(t),
\]
so
\[
\mathbb E\|z(t)\|^2=e^{-2t}\mathbb E\|x(t)\|^2.
\]
Thus the original system is mean-square exponentially stable exactly when the second moment of the \(x\)-system grows at rate strictly less than \(2\).

For each mode define conditional second moments
\[
u_i=\mathbb E[x_1^2\mathbf 1_{\sigma=i}],\qquad
v_i=\mathbb E[x_1x_2\mathbf 1_{\sigma=i}],\qquad
w_i=\mathbb E[x_2^2\mathbf 1_{\sigma=i}].
\]
Using the jump rates \(1\) between the two modes gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot u_1&=2av_1-u_1+u_2,&
\dot v_1&=aw_1-v_1+v_2,&
\dot w_1&=-w_1+w_2,\\
\dot u_2&=-u_2+u_1,&
\dot v_2&=bu_2-v_2+v_1,&
\dot w_2&=2bv_2-w_2+w_1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(\lambda\) be the Perron eigenvalue of this Metzler irreducible system. Since the matrix has nonnegative off-diagonal entries and is irreducible, its spectral abscissa is a real eigenvalue with a positive eigenvector.

For an eigenvector, set \(c=\lambda+1\). The equations become
\[
\begin{aligned}
cu_1&=2av_1+u_2,& cv_1&=aw_1+v_2,& cw_1&=w_2,\\
cu_2&=u_1,& cv_2&=bu_2+v_1,& cw_2&=2bv_2+w_1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Eliminating \(u_1,u_2,w_1,w_2\), with \(p=ab\), gives
\[
(c^2-1)u_2=2av_1,\qquad (c^2-1)w_1=2bv_2,
\]
and hence
\[
cv_1=\left(1+\frac{2p}{c^2-1}\right)v_2,\qquad
cv_2=\left(1+\frac{2p}{c^2-1}\right)v_1.
\]
For the positive Perron eigenvector we have \(v_1,v_2>0\), so
\[
c=1+\frac{2p}{c^2-1}.
\]
Since \(c=\lambda+1\),
\[
(\lambda)^2(\lambda+2)=2ab.
\]
The second-moment growth rate for \(x\) is therefore the unique positive root \(\lambda\) of
\[
\lambda^2(\lambda+2)=2ab.
\]

For the original \(z\)-system, the common factor \(e^{-t}\) shifts the second-moment exponent by \(-2\). Thus mean-square exponential stability holds iff
\[
\lambda-2<0,
\]
i.e. iff
\[
\lambda<2.
\]
Using the defining equation,
\[
\lambda<2
\iff
\lambda^2(\lambda+2)<2^2(2+2)=16
\iff
2ab<16
\iff
ab<8.
\]

At \(ab=8\), the exponent is exactly \(0\), so exponential decay fails. For \(ab>8\), the second moment grows exponentially for some initial condition, so stability also fails.

\[
\boxed{\{(a,b)\in(0,\infty)^2:\ ab<8\}}
\]
